title: tmux
label: tmux
desc: Terminal multiplexer that keeps sessions alive and splits one terminal into panes.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Install tmux, open a first session and keep the config file within reach.

snippets.code:
# Debian and Ubuntu
sudo apt install tmux

# Fedora and RHEL
sudo dnf install tmux

# Arch
sudo pacman -S tmux

# Alpine
sudo apk add tmux

# macOS
brew install tmux

# Confirm the version; 3.2 and newer support terminal-features
tmux -V

# Start a named session in a project directory
tmux new-session -s work -c ~/Projects/cheatrs

# Create it detached, attach when the terminal is free
tmux new-session -d -s work -c ~/Projects/cheatrs
tmux attach-session -t work

# Attach to work if it exists, create it otherwise
tmux new-session -A -s work

# The config is read at startup; apply edits without a restart
vim ~/.tmux.conf
tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf

sections.title: Sessions
sections.description: A session owns its windows and survives the terminal that started it.

snippets.code:
C-b d          detach, the session keeps running
C-b s          list sessions, arrows and Enter to switch
C-b $          rename the current session
C-b (   C-b )  previous and next session
C-b L          jump back to the last session

tmux ls                                # every session and its window count
tmux attach -t work                    # reattach from any terminal
tmux rename-session -t work deploy     # rename while it runs
tmux kill-session -t deploy            # close one session
tmux kill-session -a -t work           # close every session except work
tmux kill-server                       # close everything on this socket

# Reuse one session from a script instead of stacking duplicates
tmux has-session -t work 2>/dev/null || tmux new-session -d -s work

# A session created for one command closes when that command ends
tmux new-session -d -s tests 'cargo test 2>&1 | tee ~/tests.log'

sections.title: Windows
sections.description: A window fills the screen and holds a layout of panes.

snippets.code:
C-b c        new window in the current directory
C-b ,        rename this window
C-b &        close it, after a confirmation
C-b n  C-b p next and previous window
C-b 3        jump to window 3
C-b l        the window you were on before
C-b w        tree of the windows in this session
C-b f        find a window by name
C-b .        move this window to another index

# Open a window already named, in a directory, running a command
tmux new-window -t work -n logs -c /var/log 'tail -f syslog'

# Send window 2 to index 5, or exchange two windows
tmux move-window -s work:2 -t work:5
tmux swap-window -s work:1 -t work:3

# The same window shown in a second session
tmux link-window -s work:1 -t backup:1

sections.title: Panes
sections.description: Panes split one window, and each pane runs its own shell.

snippets.code:
C-b %          split left and right
C-b "          split top and bottom
C-b o          next pane in order
C-b ;          the pane you were on before
C-b q          show pane numbers, press one to jump
C-b z          zoom this pane, press again to restore
C-b x          close this pane, after a confirmation
C-b {   C-b }  swap this pane with the previous or next
C-b Space      cycle the layouts

# The new pane takes 30 percent of the width
tmux split-window -h -p 30

# Fixed size: 20 columns wide, or 12 lines tall
tmux split-window -h -l 20
tmux split-window -v -l 12

# Resize the current pane ten cells to the left
tmux resize-pane -L 10

# Spread the panes evenly
tmux select-layout tiled

# Type once, run in every pane of one window
tmux set-window-option -t work:0 synchronize-panes on
tmux set-window-option -t work:0 synchronize-panes off

# Detach a pane into a window of its own
tmux break-pane -d -s work:0.1

# Move pane 0 of window 2 into window 1
tmux join-pane -s work:2.0 -t work:1

sections.title: Navigation
sections.description: The prefix turns one keystroke into a tmux command, then the next key chooses what.

snippets.code:
C-b :        command prompt, type any tmux command
C-b ?        every binding for the current mode
C-b d        detach and leave the session running
C-b t        a large clock in the pane
C-b C-o      rotate the panes in this window
C-b PageUp   scroll back into the history

C-b C-b      send a literal C-b to the program in the pane
C-b Left     move to the pane on the left
C-b Right    move to the pane on the right
C-b Up       move to the pane above
C-b Down     move to the pane below

# What the prefix is bound to, and what copy mode does
tmux list-keys -T prefix
tmux list-keys -T copy-mode-vi

# Where am I? Print it instead of reading the status bar
tmux display-message -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}'
tmux display-message -p '#{client_width}x#{client_height}'

# Search the command table
tmux list-commands | grep split

sections.title: Copy Mode
sections.description: Copy mode freezes the pane so its scrollback can be read and selected.

snippets.code:
C-b [        enter copy mode
q  Escape    leave it
Space        start a selection
Enter        copy the selection and leave copy mode
C-b ]        paste the newest buffer into the pane
C-b =        pick a buffer to paste
C-b #        list every buffer

# vi keys instead of the emacs defaults
tmux set-window-option -g mode-keys vi

# Let the terminal handle OSC 52, so a plain copy reaches the clipboard
tmux set-option -g set-clipboard on

# Or hand the selection to the desktop clipboard on the way out
tmux bind-key -T copy-mode-vi y send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "wl-copy"

v            start a character selection
V            select whole lines
y            copy and leave copy mode
/ or ?       search, n and N for the next and previous hit
g  G         top and bottom of the history
C-u  C-d     half a page up and down

sections.title: Configuration
sections.description: Every option and binding lives in one file that is read at startup.

snippets.code:
# The file tmux reads at startup, and how to reapply it
vim ~/.tmux.conf
tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf

# What is active right now
tmux show-options -g
tmux show-window-options -g

# Start with no config at all, to see the defaults
tmux -f /dev/null new-session -s scratch

# A more comfortable prefix, with C-b still reachable
set -g prefix C-a
unbind C-b
bind C-a send-prefix

# Faster escape for vim, deeper scrollback, real mouse support
set -s escape-time 10
set -g history-limit 50000
set -g mouse on

# Count from one, like the keyboard does
set -g base-index 1
set-window-option -g pane-base-index 1
set -g renumber-windows on

# Correct terminfo for the applications inside tmux
set -g default-terminal "tmux-256color"
set -as terminal-features ",xterm-256color:RGB"

# Apply edits from inside tmux; the backslash keeps \; in one command
bind r source-file ~/.tmux.conf \; display-message "config reloaded"

# Per-machine overrides, loaded only when the file exists
if-shell "test -f ~/.tmux.local" "source-file ~/.tmux.local"

sections.title: Status Bar
sections.description: Two format strings and a window list, refreshed on a timer.

snippets.code:
# Dark bar, refreshed every five seconds
set -g status-style "bg=colour235,fg=colour250"
set -g status-interval 5

# Room for long session names and a full clock
set -g status-left-length 40
set -g status-right-length 60

# #S is the session, #I the window index, #W its name, #P the pane
set -g status-left "#[bg=colour34,fg=colour232,bold] #S #[fg=colour250,bg=colour235] "

# Current command, a prefix indicator and the time
set -g status-right "#[fg=colour250]#{pane_current_command} #{?client_prefix,#[fg=colour160]PREFIX ,}#[fg=colour34]%H:%M"

# Window tabs: index and name, highlighted when current
set-window-option -g window-status-format " #I:#W "
set-window-option -g window-status-current-format "#[bg=colour34,fg=colour232,bold] #I:#W "
set-window-option -g window-status-separator ""

# Mark windows that changed while you were elsewhere
set-window-option -g monitor-activity on
set -g visual-activity on

sections.title: Scripting
sections.description: Every action is a command, so a shell script can build and drive a layout.

snippets.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

name=dev

if ! tmux has-session -t "$name" 2>/dev/null; then
  tmux new-session -d -s "$name" -c "$HOME/Projects/cheatrs"
  tmux new-window  -t "$name" -n server
  tmux new-window  -t "$name" -n tests
  tmux select-window -t "$name:1"
fi

tmux attach-session -t "$name"

# Type into a specific pane; C-m is Enter
tmux send-keys -t dev:0.1 'cargo watch -x test' C-m

# Read the last 200 lines of a pane without attaching
tmux capture-pane -p -t dev:0.1 -S -200 | tail -n 20

# List every pane with its working directory
tmux list-panes -a -F '#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index} #{pane_current_path}'

# Two splits, then an even grid
tmux split-window -t dev:0 -h
tmux split-window -t dev:0 -v
tmux select-layout -t dev:0 tiled

# Wait for a background job instead of sleeping
tmux new-session -d -s build 'cargo build --release; tmux wait-for -S build-done'
tmux wait-for build-done
tmux kill-session -t build

# Ask tmux for a value in a script
socket=$(tmux display-message -p '#{socket_path}')
echo "tmux socket: $socket"

sections.title: Plugins
sections.description: TPM clones, loads and updates the plugins declared in the config.

snippets.code:
# The plugin manager is cloned once, outside the config
git clone https://github.com/tmux-plugins/tpm ~/.tmux/plugins/tpm

# Declared at the end of ~/.tmux.conf, before the run line
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tpm'
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-sensible'
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-resurrect'
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-continuum'
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-yank'

# Restore the layout after a reboot and keep the scrollback
set -g @continuum-restore 'on'
set -g @resurrect-capture-pane-contents 'on'

run '~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/tpm'

# Inside tmux: prefix + I installs, prefix + U updates, prefix + M-u removes

# The same actions from a shell
~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/install_plugins
~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/update_plugins all
~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/clean_plugins
